bib.title: TheoremQA: A Theorem-driven Question Answering Dataset

question: Can LLMs apply university-level theorems to solve challenging science problems, which grade-school math benchmarks no longer test?
hypothesis: Existing math word problem sets are too easy and not theorem-driven, so a theorem-based set will separate strong from weak LLMs.
contributions: First theorem-driven QA dataset to test LLMs' ability to apply science theorems
Analyses of theorem integration and multimodal understanding

method.summary: Experts collected 800 university-level questions over 354 theorems in Math, Physics, EE&CS and Finance, rewriting each so the answer is an integer, float, list, bool or option. 16 LLMs were prompted with CoT and PoT; answers were extracted with ChatGPT and normalised with WolframAlpha.

datasets.name: TheoremQA
datasets.size: 800 questions, 354 theorems, 51 image questions (text elsewhere says 50)
datasets.split: single evaluation set, no train/dev split stated
datasets.source: Websites, books, or written by nine domain experts; theorem list first drafted by GPT-4 then refined by experts (~400 theorems enumerated); licence not stated
datasets.preprocessing: Experts modified web questions to reduce contamination and to force answers into integer/float/list/bool/option

models.name: Alpaca-13B, Vicuna-13B (LLaMA); OpenAssistant-12B (Pythia); MOSS-instruct-16B (CodeGen); StarChat-16B (StarCoder); InstructCodeT5+ (16B in Table 2)

inference.prompting: CoT and PoT; one demonstration example for GPT-3 and GPT-3.5 (non-chat) to fix the output format; GPT-4 case study says it worked without any demonstration; number of shots otherwise not stated
inference.retrieval: Optional theorem augmentation: GPT-4-written theorem description (post-processed) or web-retrieved description concatenated in the prompt

parameters.multimodal: BLIP captions of images appended to the prompt (Chameleon style)
parameters.answer_extraction: ChatGPT finds the answer span, WolframAlpha normalises to float/integer/list

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction of questions whose extracted and normalised answer matches the ground truth, broken down by answer type and field

eval.protocol: single run per model and prompt as far as stated; no seeds, no significance test; extractor is imperfect so accuracy is an approximate lower bound

evidence.quote: we also include 51 questions with image input (diagrams)

limits: Answer extraction is imperfect so reported accuracy is an approximate lower bound (authors)
Questions with formula, figure or matrix answers were deliberately avoided, which biases coverage (authors)
No multimodal model succeeded on the image subset (authors)
No contamination test, only an instruction to experts to modify questions; GPT-4 also helped draft the theorem list
Decoding settings, temperature, shot count and seeds are not reported
Small per-field counts (Finance 81, Physics 131) and a single run mean wide uncertainty; no confidence intervals
Headline 51% in abstract differs from 52.4 in Table 2; 350/354 theorems and 50/51 image questions printed inconsistently
